Ecopetrol SA Posts Higher Quarterly Earnings on Strong Output, Stable Oil Prices

BOGOTÁ, June 28 — Ecopetrol SA, Colombia’s largest oil and gas producer, reported higher quarterly earnings on Friday, buoyed by steady crude output and resilient international oil prices.

The company posted a net income of 6.2 trillion pesos ($1.6 billion) for the first quarter, up 12% from 5.5 trillion pesos a year earlier. Revenues rose 9% year-on-year to 32.7 trillion pesos, as average production reached 735,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day, surpassing company targets.

CEO Felipe Bayón said in a statement, “Consistent operational performance and disciplined cost management allowed us to deliver solid results, despite a volatile macroeconomic environment.”

Ecopetrol benefited from Brent crude prices averaging $83 per barrel during the quarter, easing concerns about the impact of global supply fluctuations. The company’s refining and transport units also contributed to the positive results, with refining margins stable due to robust domestic fuel demand.

Analysts noted the company’s improved efficiency. “Ecopetrol’s continued focus on cost controls and incremental output is positioning it well as Colombia’s energy sector faces uncertainty over future exploration policies,” said Ana María Castillo, energy analyst at Bogota Capital Advisors.

Ecopetrol confirmed it will maintain its 2024 investment guidance of $5.2 billion to $6.5 billion, with a focus on upstream projects and growth in natural gas. The company also reaffirmed its commitment to sustainable development, citing progress on emissions reduction and water management.

The company plans to pay an interim dividend of 243 pesos per share, in line with its dividend policy.

Shares of Ecopetrol closed up 1.3% on the Bogotá Stock Exchange ahead of the results announcement.
